2572    def explode_infos(
2573        self,
2574        prefix: str = None,
2575        create_index: bool = False,
2576        fields: list = None,
2577        fields_just_add: list = [],
2578        fields_not_exists: bool = True,
2579        detect_type_list: bool = True,
2580        force: bool = False,
2581        proccess_all_fields_together: bool = False,
2582        fields_forced_as_varchar: bool = False,
2583        table: str = None,
2584        table_source: str = None,
2585        table_dest: str = None,
2586        table_key: list = None,
2587    ) -> list:
2588        """
2589        Explode the INFO fields of a VCF file into individual columns in a specified table.
2590
2591        Args:
2592            prefix (str, optional): A prefix for the exploded INFO fields. If not provided, the function
2593                will use the value of `self.get_explode_infos_prefix()`.
2594            create_index (bool, optional): Whether to create indexes on the exploded INFO fields. Defaults to False.
2595            fields (list, optional): A list of INFO fields to explode into individual columns. If not provided,
2596                all INFO fields will be exploded.
2597            fields_just_add (list, optional): A list of INFO fields to add as individual columns without exploding values.
2598            fields_not_exists (bool, optional): Whether to add fields that do not exist in the table. Defaults to True.
2599            detect_type_list (bool, optional): Whether to detect if the field is a list type. Defaults to True.
2600            force (bool, optional): Whether to drop and recreate a column if it already exists in the table. Defaults to False.
2601            proccess_all_fields_together (bool, optional): Whether to process all INFO fields together or individually.
2602                Defaults to False.
2603            fields_forced_as_varchar (bool, optional): Whether to force all fields to be treated as VARCHAR. Defaults to False.
2604            table (str, optional): The name of the table where the exploded INFO fields will be added as individual columns.
2605            table_source (str, optional): The name of the source table containing the INFO fields.
2606            table_dest (str, optional): The name of the destination table where the exploded INFO fields will be added.
2607            table_key (list, optional): A list of keys to use for identifying rows in the table.
2608
2609        Returns:
2610            list: A list of added columns.
2611        """
2612
2613        # drop indexes
2614        self.drop_indexes()
2615
2616        # connexion format
2617        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
2618        if connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
2619            msg_err = (
2620                f"Connexion format '{connexion_format}' not available for explode infos"
2621            )
2622            log.error(msg_err)
2623            raise ValueError(msg_err)
2624
2625        # Access
2626        # access = self.get_config().get("access", None)
2627        access = self.get_access(default=None)
2628
2629        # Added columns
2630        added_columns = []
2631
2632        if access not in ["RO"]:
2633
2634            # Translate fields if patterns
2635            fields = self.get_explode_infos_fields(explode_infos_fields=fields)
2636
2637            if fields is None or len(fields) == 0:
2638                return []
2639
2640            # prefix
2641            if prefix in [None, True] or not isinstance(prefix, str):
2642                if self.get_explode_infos_prefix() not in [None, True]:
2643                    prefix = self.get_explode_infos_prefix()
2644                else:
2645                    prefix = "INFO/"
2646
2647            # table variants
2648            if table is None:
2649                table = self.get_table_variants(clause="select")
2650
2651            # table source
2652            if table_source is None:
2653                table_source = table
2654
2655            # table dest
2656            if table_dest is None:
2657                table_dest = table
2658
2659            # table key
2660            if table_key is None:
2661                table_key = ["#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT"]
2662
2663            # Check source table columns
2664            try:
2665                table_source_struct = self.get_columns(table=table_source)
2666            except:
2667                table_source_struct = []
2668            try:
2669                table_dest_struct = self.get_columns(table=table_dest)
2670            except:
2671                table_dest_struct = []
2672
2673            if "INFO" not in table_source_struct:
2674                msg_err = f"Column 'INFO' not found in table '{table_source}'"
2675                log.warning(msg_err)
2676                # return None
2677                # raise ValueError(msg_err)
2678
2679            # Header infos
2680            header_infos = self.get_header().infos
2681
2682            log.debug(
2683                f"Explode INFO fields - [{len(header_infos)}] annotations fields in header"
2684            )
2685
2686            # Create view with all fields
2687            view_source = "view_source_" + str(random.randint(10000, 100000))
2688            view_source = self.create_annotations_view(
2689                table=table_source,
2690                fields=fields,
2691                view=view_source,
2692                view_type="view",
2693                view_mode="explore",
2694                info_prefix_column=prefix,
2695                fields_needed=table_key,
2696                fields_not_exists=fields_not_exists,
2697                fields_forced_as_varchar=fields_forced_as_varchar,
2698                detect_type_list=detect_type_list,
2699            )
2700
2701            # Describe view source
2702            describe_query = f"DESCRIBE {view_source}"
2703            res = self.execute_query(describe_query)
2704            description_dict = {row[0]: {"type": row[1]} for row in res.fetchall()}
2705
2706            # View source structure
2707            view_source_struct = self.get_columns(table=view_source)
2708
2709            # Set fields
2710            sql_info_alter_table_array = []
2711
2712            for info in fields:
2713
2714                info_id_sql = prefix + info
2715
2716                if info_id_sql in table_dest_struct:
2717                    log.debug(f"Field '{info_id_sql}' already exists in table")
2718
2719                if (
2720                    info_id_sql in view_source_struct
2721                    and "INFO" in table_source_struct
2722                    and (info_id_sql not in table_dest_struct or force)
2723                ):
2724
2725                    if "INFO" not in table_source_struct:
2726                        msg_err = f"Column 'INFO' not found in table '{table_source}' - Column 'INFO' needed!!!"
2727                        log.error(msg_err)
2728                        raise ValueError(msg_err)
2729
2730                    if info_id_sql in table_dest_struct and force:
2731                        log.debug(
2732                            f"Explode INFO fields - Force '{info}' annotations fields update from 'INFO' column"
2733                        )
2734
2735                    log.debug(f"Explode INFO fields - ADD '{info}' annotations fields")
2736
2737                    # Get field type
2738                    type_sql = description_dict.get(info_id_sql, {})["type"]
2739
2740                    # Add field
2741                    added_column = self.add_column(
2742                        table_name=table_dest,
2743                        column_name=info_id_sql,
2744                        column_type=type_sql,
2745                        default_value="null",
2746                        drop=force,
2747                    )
2748
2749                    # Added column
2750                    if added_column:
2751                        added_columns.append(added_column)
2752                        log.debug(
2753                            f"Explode INFO fields - ADD '{info}' annotations fields - added"
2754                        )
2755                    else:
2756                        log.debug(
2757                            f"Explode INFO fields - ADD '{info}' annotations fields - not added"
2758                        )
2759
2760                    # if added_column or force: #fileds_just_add
2761                    if (added_column or force) and not info in fields_just_add:
2762
2763                        # add field to index
2764                        self.index_additionnal_fields.append(info_id_sql)
2765
2766                        update_info_field = f"""
2767                            "{info_id_sql}" = {view_source}."{info_id_sql}"
2768                            """
2769
2770                        # Set field append
2771                        sql_info_alter_table_array.append(update_info_field)
2772
2773            if sql_info_alter_table_array:
2774
2775                # Where clause join
2776                where_clause_join = f"""
2777                    {" AND ".join([f'"{table_dest}"."{key}" = "{view_source}"."{key}"' for key in table_key])}
2778                """
2779
2780                # Evaluate block size
2781                batch_split = self.get_batch_split()
2782
2783                # Insert by batch
2784                for batch_index in range(batch_split):
2785
2786                    log.debug(
2787                        f"Explode INFO fields - Process batch [{batch_index+1}/{batch_split}]..."
2788                    )
2789
2790                    where_clause = where_clause_join
2791
2792                    # where clause
2793                    if batch_split > 1:
2794                        where_clause += (
2795                            f" AND ({table_dest}.POS % {batch_split}) = {batch_index} "
2796                        )
2797                    else:
2798                        where_clause += ""
2799
2800                    # Update table
2801                    if proccess_all_fields_together:
2802                        sql_info_alter_table_array_join = ", ".join(
2803                            sql_info_alter_table_array
2804                        )
2805                        if sql_info_alter_table_array_join:
2806                            sql_info_alter_table = f"""
2807                                UPDATE {table_dest}
2808                                SET {sql_info_alter_table_array_join}
2809                                FROM {view_source}
2810                                WHERE {where_clause}
2811                                """
2812                            log.debug(
2813                                f"Explode INFO fields - Explode all {len(sql_info_alter_table_array)} fields..."
2814                            )
2815                            # log.debug(sql_info_alter_table)
2816                            self.conn.execute(sql_info_alter_table)
2817                    else:
2818                        sql_info_alter_num = 0
2819                        for sql_info_alter in sql_info_alter_table_array:
2820                            sql_info_alter_num += 1
2821                            sql_info_alter_table = f"""
2822                                UPDATE {table_dest}
2823                                SET {sql_info_alter}
2824                                FROM {view_source}
2825                                WHERE {where_clause}
2826                                """
2827                            log.debug(
2828                                f"Explode INFO fields - Explode field {sql_info_alter_num}/{len(sql_info_alter_table_array)}..."
2829                            )
2830                            # log.debug(sql_info_alter_table)
2831                            self.conn.execute(sql_info_alter_table)
2832
2833            # Remove view_source
2834            self.remove_tables_or_views(tables=[view_source])
2835
2836        # create indexes
2837        if create_index:
2838            self.create_indexes()
2839
2840        return added_columns
2841
2842    def create_indexes(self) -> None:
2843        """
2844        Create indexes on the table after insertion
2845        """
2846
2847        # Access
2848        # access = self.get_config().get("access", None)
2849        access = self.get_access(default=None)
2850
2851        # get table variants
2852        table_variants = self.get_table_variants("FROM")
2853
2854        if self.get_indexing() and access not in ["RO"]:
2855            # Create index
2856            sql_create_table_index = f'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_{self.get_table_variants()} ON {table_variants} ("#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT")'
2857            self.conn.execute(sql_create_table_index)
2858            sql_create_table_index = f'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_{self.get_table_variants()}_chrom ON {table_variants} ("#CHROM")'
2859            self.conn.execute(sql_create_table_index)
2860            sql_create_table_index = f'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_{self.get_table_variants()}_pos ON {table_variants} ("POS")'
2861            self.conn.execute(sql_create_table_index)
2862            sql_create_table_index = f'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_{self.get_table_variants()}_ref ON {table_variants} ( "REF")'
2863            self.conn.execute(sql_create_table_index)
2864            sql_create_table_index = f'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_{self.get_table_variants()}_alt ON {table_variants} ("ALT")'
2865            self.conn.execute(sql_create_table_index)
2866            for field in self.index_additionnal_fields:
2867                sql_create_table_index = f""" CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_{self.get_table_variants()}_{field}" ON {table_variants} ("{field}") """
2868                self.conn.execute(sql_create_table_index)
2869
2870    def drop_indexes(self) -> None:
2871        """
2872        Create indexes on the table after insertion
2873        """
2874
2875        # Access
2876        # access = self.get_config().get("access", None)
2877        access = self.get_access(default=None)
2878
2879        # get table variants
2880        table_variants = self.get_table_variants("FROM")
2881
2882        # Get database format
2883        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
2884
2885        if access not in ["RO"]:
2886            if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
2887                sql_list_indexes = f"SELECT index_name FROM duckdb_indexes WHERE table_name='{table_variants}'"
2888            elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
2889                sql_list_indexes = f"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index' AND tbl_name='{table_variants}';"
2890
2891            list_indexes = self.conn.execute(sql_list_indexes)
2892            index_names = [row[0] for row in list_indexes.fetchall()]
2893            for index in index_names:
2894                sql_drop_table_index = f""" DROP INDEX IF EXISTS "{index}" """
2895                self.conn.execute(sql_drop_table_index)
2896
2897    def read_vcf_header(self, f) -> list:
2898        """
2899        It reads the header of a VCF file and returns a list of the header lines
2900
2901        :param f: the file object
2902        :return: The header lines of the VCF file.
2903        """
2904
2905        header_list = []
2906        for line in f:
2907            header_list.append(line)
2908            if line.startswith("#CHROM"):
2909                break
2910        return header_list
2911
2912    def read_vcf_header_file(self, file: str = None) -> list:
2913        """
2914        The `read_vcf_header_file` function reads the header of a VCF file, handling both compressed and
2915        uncompressed files.
2916
2917        :param file: The `file` parameter is a string that represents the path to the VCF header file
2918        that you want to read. It is an optional parameter, so if you don't provide a value, it will
2919        default to `None`
2920        :type file: str
2921        :return: The function `read_vcf_header_file` returns a list.
2922        """
2923
2924        if self.get_input_compressed(input_file=file):
2925            with bgzf.open(file, "rt") as f:
2926                return self.read_vcf_header(f=f)
2927        else:
2928            with open(file, "rt") as f:
2929                return self.read_vcf_header(f=f)

2931    def execute_query(self, query: str):
2932        """
2933        It takes a query as an argument, executes it, and returns the results
2934
2935        :param query: The query to be executed
2936        :return: The result of the query is being returned.
2937        """
2938        if query:
2939            return self.conn.execute(query)  # .fetchall()
2940        else:
2941            return None

2943    def export_output(
2944        self,
2945        output_file: str | None = None,
2946        output_header: str | None = None,
2947        export_header: bool = True,
2948        explode_infos: bool = True,
2949        header_in_output: bool = None,
2950        query: str | None = None,
2951        parquet_partitions: list | None = None,
2952        chunk_size: int | None = None,
2953        threads: int | None = None,
2954        sort: bool = False,
2955        index: bool = False,
2956        order_by: str | None = None,
2957        fields_to_rename: dict | None = None,
2958        force_cast_as_flat: bool = False,
2959    ) -> bool:
2960        """
2961        The `export_output` function exports data from a VCF file to various formats, including VCF,
2962        CSV, TSV, PSV, and Parquet, with options for customization such as filtering, sorting, and
2963        partitioning.
2964
2965        :param output_file: The `output_file` parameter is a string that specifies the name of the
2966        output file where the exported data will be saved
2967        :type output_file: str | None
2968        :param output_header: The `output_header` parameter is a string that specifies the name of the
2969        file where the header of the VCF file will be exported. If this parameter is not provided, the
2970        header will be exported to a file with the same name as the `output_file` parameter, but with
2971        the extension "
2972        :type output_header: str | None
2973        :param export_header: The `export_header` parameter is a boolean flag that determines whether
2974        the header of a VCF file should be exported to a separate file or not. If `export_header` is
2975        True, the header will be exported to a file. If `export_header` is False, the header will not
2976        be, defaults to True
2977        :type export_header: bool (optional)
2978        :param explode_infos: The `explode_infos` parameter is a boolean flag that determines whether
2979        the INFO fields in the VCF file should be exploded into individual columns in the output file.
2980        If `explode_infos` is set to True, the INFO fields will be exploded. If `explode_infos` is set
2981        to False, the INFO fields will not be exploded. By default, the INFO fields are exploded
2982        :type explode_infos: bool (optional)
2983        :param query: The `query` parameter in the `export_output` function is an optional SQL query
2984        that can be used to filter and select specific data from the VCF file before exporting it. If
2985        provided, only the data that matches the query will be exported. This allows you to customize
2986        the exported data based on
2987        :type query: str | None
2988        :param header_in_output: The `header_in_output` parameter is a boolean flag that determines
2989        whether the header should be included in the output file. If `header_in_output` is set to `True`,
2990        the header will be included in the output file. If `header_in_output` is set to `False`, the
2991        header will not be included in the output file. By default, the header is included in the output
2992        file
2993        :type header_in_output: bool (optional)
2994        :param parquet_partitions: The `parquet_partitions` parameter is a list that specifies the
2995        columns to be used for partitioning the Parquet file during export. Partitioning is a way to
2996        organize data in a hierarchical directory structure based on the values of one or more columns.
2997        This can improve query performance when working with large datasets
2998        :type parquet_partitions: list | None
2999        :param chunk_size: The `chunk_size` parameter specifies the number of records in a batch when
3000        exporting data in Parquet format. This parameter is used for partitioning the Parquet file into
3001        multiple files. It helps in optimizing the export process by breaking down the data into
3002        manageable chunks for processing and storage
3003        :type chunk_size: int | None
3004        :param threads: The `threads` parameter in the `export_output` function specifies the number of
3005        threads to be used during the export process. It determines the level of parallelism and can
3006        improve the performance of the export operation. If this parameter is not provided, the function
3007        will use the default number of threads
3008        :type threads: int | None
3009        :param sort: The `sort` parameter in the `export_output` function is a boolean flag that
3010        determines whether the output file should be sorted based on genomic coordinates of the
3011        variants. If `sort` is set to `True`, the output file will be sorted. If `sort` is set to
3012        `False`,, defaults to False
3013        :type sort: bool (optional)
3014        :param index: The `index` parameter in the `export_output` function is a boolean flag that
3015        determines whether an index should be created on the output file. If `index` is set to `True`,
3016        an index will be created on the output file. If `index` is set to `False`, no, defaults to False
3017        :type index: bool (optional)
3018        :param order_by: The `order_by` parameter in the `export_output` function is a string that
3019        specifies the column(s) to use for sorting the output file. This parameter is only applicable
3020        when exporting data in VCF format. It allows you to specify the column(s) based on which the
3021        output file should be
3022        :type order_by: str | None
3023        :param fields_to_rename: The `fields_to_rename` parameter is a dictionary that specifies the
3024        mapping of field names to be renamed during the export process. This parameter allows you to
3025        customize the output field names before exporting the data. Each key-value pair in the
3026        dictionary represents the original field name as the key and the new field name
3027        :type fields_to_rename: dict | None
3028        :param force_cast_as_flat: Only for Parquet format. The `force_cast_as_flat` parameter is a boolean
3029        flag that determines whether to force the export of nested or complex data structures as flat
3030        structures. If `force_cast_as_flat` is set to `True`, the function will flatten any nested
3031        structures in the data before exporting it. If `force_cast_as_flat` is set to `False`, the
3032        function will preserve the original structure of the data during export. By default, it is set
3033        to False
3034        :type force_cast_as_flat: bool (optional)
3035        :return: The `export_output` function returns a boolean value. It checks if the output file
3036        exists and returns True if it does, or None if it doesn't.
3037        """
3038
3039        # Log
3040        log.info("Exporting...")
3041
3042        # Full path
3043        output_file = full_path(output_file)
3044        output_header = full_path(output_header)
3045
3046        # Config
3047        config = self.get_config()
3048
3049        # Param
3050        param = self.get_param()
3051
3052        # Tmp files to remove
3053        tmp_to_remove = []
3054
3055        # If no output, get it
3056        if not output_file:
3057            output_file = self.get_output()
3058
3059        # If not threads
3060        if not threads:
3061            threads = self.get_threads()
3062
3063        # Rename fields
3064        if not fields_to_rename:
3065            fields_to_rename = param.get("export", {}).get("fields_to_rename", None)
3066        self.rename_info_fields(fields_to_rename=fields_to_rename)
3067
3068        # Force cast as flat
3069        force_cast_as_flat = param.get("export", {}).get(
3070            "force_cast_as_flat", force_cast_as_flat
3071        )
3072
3073        # Auto header name with extension
3074        if export_header or output_header:
3075            if not output_header:
3076                output_header = f"{output_file}.hdr"
3077            # Export header
3078            self.export_header(output_file=output_file, query=query)
3079
3080        # Switch off export header if VCF output
3081        output_file_type = get_file_format(output_file)
3082        if output_file_type in ["vcf"]:
3083            export_header = False
3084            tmp_to_remove.append(output_header)
3085
3086        # Chunk size
3087        if not chunk_size:
3088            chunk_size = config.get("chunk_size", None)
3089
3090        # Parquet partition
3091        if not parquet_partitions:
3092            parquet_partitions = param.get("export", {}).get("parquet_partitions", None)
3093        if parquet_partitions and isinstance(parquet_partitions, str):
3094            parquet_partitions = parquet_partitions.split(",")
3095
3096        # Order by
3097        if not order_by:
3098            order_by = param.get("export", {}).get("order_by", "")
3099
3100        # Header in output
3101        if header_in_output is None:
3102            header_in_output = param.get("export", {}).get("include_header", False)
3103
3104        # Database
3105        database_source = self.get_connexion()
3106
3107        # Connexion format
3108        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
3109
3110        # Explode infos
3111        if self.get_explode_infos() and explode_infos:
3112            self.explode_infos(
3113                prefix=self.get_explode_infos_prefix(),
3114                fields=self.get_explode_infos_fields(),
3115                force=False,
3116                fields_forced_as_varchar=True,
3117            )
3118
3119        # if connexion_format in ["sqlite"] or query:
3120        if connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
3121
3122            # Export in Parquet
3123            random_tmp = "".join(
3124                random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for i in range(10)
3125            )
3126            database_source = f"""{output_file}.{random_tmp}.database_export.parquet"""
3127            tmp_to_remove.append(database_source)
3128
3129            # Table Variants
3130            table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
3131
3132            # Create export query
3133            sql_query_export_subquery = f"""
3134                SELECT * FROM {table_variants}
3135                """
3136
3137            # Write source file
3138            fp.write(database_source, self.get_query_to_df(sql_query_export_subquery))
3139
3140        # Create database
3141        database = Database(
3142            database=database_source,
3143            table="variants",
3144            header_file=output_header,
3145            conn_config=self.get_connexion_config(),
3146        )
3147
3148        # Existing colomns header
3149        existing_columns_header = database.get_header_columns_from_database(query=query)
3150
3151        # Sample list
3152        if output_file_type in ["vcf"]:
3153            get_samples = self.get_samples()
3154            get_samples_check = self.get_samples_check()
3155            samples_force = get_samples is not None
3156            sample_list = self.get_header_sample_list(
3157                check=get_samples_check,
3158                samples=get_samples,
3159                samples_force=samples_force,
3160            )
3161        else:
3162            sample_list = None
3163
3164        # Export file
3165        database.export(
3166            output_database=output_file,
3167            output_header=output_header,
3168            existing_columns_header=existing_columns_header,
3169            parquet_partitions=parquet_partitions,
3170            chunk_size=chunk_size,
3171            threads=threads,
3172            sort=sort,
3173            index=index,
3174            header_in_output=header_in_output,
3175            order_by=order_by,
3176            query=query,
3177            export_header=export_header,
3178            sample_list=sample_list,
3179            force_cast_as_flat=force_cast_as_flat,
3180        )
3181
3182        # Remove
3183        remove_if_exists(tmp_to_remove)
3184
3185        return (os.path.exists(output_file) or None) and (
3186            os.path.exists(output_file) or None
3187        )

3189    def get_columns(self, table: str = None) -> list:
3190        """
3191        The `get_columns` function returns a list of columns in a specified table. If the `table`
3192        parameter is not provided when calling the function, it will default to using the variants table.
3193
3194        Args:
3195            table (str, optional): The name of the table from which you want to retrieve the columns. If not provided,
3196                it will default to using the variants table.
3197
3198        Returns:
3199            list: A list of columns in the specified table.
3200        """
3201
3202        if not table:
3203            table = self.get_table_variants()
3204
3205        # Use PRAGMA table_info for SQLite or DESCRIBE for other databases
3206        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
3207        if connexion_format == "sqlite":
3208            query = f"PRAGMA table_info({table})"
3209            columns_info = self.get_query_to_df(query)
3210            columns = columns_info["name"].tolist()
3211        else:
3212            query = f"DESCRIBE {table}"
3213            columns_info = self.get_query_to_df(query)
3214            columns = columns_info["column_name"].tolist()
3215
3216        return columns
3217
3218    def get_extra_infos(self, table: str = None) -> list:
3219        """
3220        The `get_extra_infos` function returns a list of columns that are in a specified table but not
3221        in the header.
3222
3223        :param table: The `table` parameter in the `get_extra_infos` function is used to specify the
3224        name of the table from which you want to retrieve the extra columns that are not present in the
3225        header. If the `table` parameter is not provided when calling the function, it will default to
3226        using the variants
3227        :type table: str
3228        :return: A list of columns that are in the specified table but not in the header of the table.
3229        """
3230
3231        header_columns = []
3232
3233        if not table:
3234            table = self.get_table_variants(clause="from")
3235            header_columns = self.get_header_columns()
3236
3237        # Check all columns in the database
3238        query = f""" SELECT * FROM {table} LIMIT 1 """
3239        log.debug(f"query {query}")
3240        table_columns = self.get_query_to_df(query).columns.tolist()
3241        extra_columns = []
3242
3243        # Construct extra infos (not in header)
3244        for column in table_columns:
3245            if column not in header_columns:
3246                extra_columns.append(column)
3247
3248        return extra_columns
3249
3250    def get_extra_infos_sql(self, table: str = None) -> str:
3251        """
3252        It returns a string of the extra infos, separated by commas, and each extra info is surrounded
3253        by double quotes
3254
3255        :param table: The name of the table to get the extra infos from. If None, the default table is
3256        used
3257        :type table: str
3258        :return: A string of the extra infos
3259        """
3260
3261        return ", ".join(
3262            ['"' + str(elem) + '"' for elem in self.get_extra_infos(table=table)]
3263        )

3265    def export_header(
3266        self,
3267        header_name: str = None,
3268        output_file: str = None,
3269        output_file_ext: str = ".hdr",
3270        clean_header: bool = True,
3271        clean_info_flag: bool = False,
3272        remove_chrom_line: bool = False,
3273        query: str | None = None,
3274    ) -> str:
3275        """
3276        The `export_header` function takes a VCF file, extracts the header, modifies it according to
3277        specified options, and writes it to a new file.
3278
3279        :param header_name: The `header_name` parameter is the name of the header file to be created. If
3280        this parameter is not specified, the header will be written to the output file
3281        :type header_name: str
3282        :param output_file: The `output_file` parameter in the `export_header` function is used to
3283        specify the name of the output file where the header will be written. If this parameter is not
3284        provided, the header will be written to a temporary file
3285        :type output_file: str
3286        :param output_file_ext: The `output_file_ext` parameter in the `export_header` function is a
3287        string that represents the extension of the output header file. By default, it is set to ".hdr"
3288        if not specified by the user. This extension will be appended to the `output_file` name to
3289        create the final, defaults to .hdr
3290        :type output_file_ext: str (optional)
3291        :param clean_header: The `clean_header` parameter in the `export_header` function is a boolean
3292        flag that determines whether the header should be cleaned or not. When `clean_header` is set to
3293        `True`, the function will clean the header by modifying certain lines based on a specific
3294        pattern. If `clean_header`, defaults to True
3295        :type clean_header: bool (optional)
3296        :param clean_info_flag: The `clean_info_flag` parameter in the `export_header` function is a boolean
3297        flag that determines whether the header should be cleaned for INFO/tags that are 'Flag' type.
3298        When `clean_info_flag` is set to `True`, the function will replace INFO/tags 'Type' as 'String'.
3299        Default to False
3300        :type clean_info_flag: bool (optional)
3301        :param remove_chrom_line: The `remove_chrom_line` parameter in the `export_header` function is a
3302        boolean flag that determines whether the #CHROM line should be removed from the header before
3303        writing it to the output file. If set to `True`, the #CHROM line will be removed; if set to `,
3304        defaults to False
3305        :type remove_chrom_line: bool (optional)
3306        :param query: The `query` parameter in the `export_header` function is an optional SQL query
3307        string that can be used to filter the columns in the header. If provided, the function will
3308        retrieve only the columns that match the query. If not provided, all columns in the header will
3309        be included in the output
3310        :type query: str | None
3311        :return: The function `export_header` returns the name of the temporary header file that is
3312        created.
3313        """
3314
3315        if not header_name and not output_file:
3316            output_file = self.get_output()
3317
3318        if self.get_header():
3319
3320            # Get header object
3321            header_obj = self.get_header()
3322
3323            # Create database
3324            db_for_header = Database(database=self.get_input())
3325
3326            # Get real columns in the file
3327            db_header_columns = db_for_header.get_columns(sql_query=query)
3328
3329            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
3330
3331                # Write header file
3332                header_file_tmp = os.path.join(tmpdir, "header")
3333                f = open(header_file_tmp, "w")
3334                vcf.Writer(f, header_obj)
3335                f.close()
3336
3337                # Replace #CHROM line with rel columns
3338                header_list = db_for_header.read_header_file(
3339                    header_file=header_file_tmp
3340                )
3341                header_list[-1] = "\t".join(db_header_columns)
3342
3343                # Remove CHROM line
3344                if remove_chrom_line:
3345                    header_list.pop()
3346
3347                # Clean header
3348                if clean_header:
3349                    header_list_clean = []
3350                    for head in header_list:
3351                        # Clean head for malformed header
3352                        head_clean = head
3353                        if clean_info_flag:
3354                            head_clean = re.subn(
3355                                "##FORMAT=<ID=(.*),Number=(.*),Type=Flag",
3356                                r"##FORMAT=<ID=\1,Number=\2,Type=String",
3357                                head_clean,
3358                                2,
3359                            )[0]
3360                        # Write header
3361                        header_list_clean.append(head_clean)
3362                    header_list = header_list_clean
3363
3364            tmp_header_name = output_file + output_file_ext
3365
3366            f = open(tmp_header_name, "w")
3367            for line in header_list:
3368                f.write(line)
3369            f.close()
3370
3371        return tmp_header_name
3372
3373    def export_variant_vcf(
3374        self,
3375        vcf_file,
3376        remove_info: bool = False,
3377        add_samples: bool = True,
3378        list_samples: list = [],
3379        where_clause: str = "",
3380        sort: bool = True,
3381        index: bool = False,
3382        threads: int | None = None,
3383    ) -> bool | None:
3384        """
3385        The `export_variant_vcf` function exports a VCF file with specified samples, allowing options to
3386        remove INFO field, add samples, and control compression and indexing.
3387
3388        :param vcf_file: The `vcf_file` parameter is the name of the file where the VCF data will be
3389        written to. It is the output file that will contain the filtered VCF data based on the specified
3390        parameters
3391        :param remove_info: The `remove_info` parameter in the `export_variant_vcf` function is a
3392        boolean flag that determines whether to remove the INFO field from the output VCF file. If set
3393        to `True`, the INFO field will be removed. If set to `False`, the INFO field will be included
3394        in, defaults to False
3395        :type remove_info: bool (optional)
3396        :param add_samples: The `add_samples` parameter is a boolean parameter that determines whether
3397        the samples should be added to the VCF file or not. If set to True, the samples will be added.
3398        If set to False, the samples will be removed. The default value is True, defaults to True
3399        :type add_samples: bool (optional)
3400        :param list_samples: The `list_samples` parameter is a list of samples that you want to include
3401        in the output VCF file. By default, all samples will be included. If you provide a list of
3402        samples, only those samples will be included in the output file
3403        :type list_samples: list
3404        :param where_clause: The `where_clause` parameter in the `export_variant_vcf` function is a
3405        string that represents a SQL WHERE clause. It is used to filter the variants that will be
3406        exported to the VCF file. The `where_clause` allows you to specify conditions that the variants
3407        must meet in order to be included in the output VCF file. If no `where_clause` is provided, all
3408        variants will be exported
3409        :type where_clause: str
3410        :param sort: The `sort` parameter in the `export_variant_vcf` function is a boolean flag that
3411        determines whether the output VCF file should be sorted based on genomic coordinates of the variants.
3412        If `sort` is set to `True`, the output VCF file will be sorted. If `sort` is set to `False`, the output VCF file
3413        will not be sorted. By default, the output VCF file is sorted
3414        :type sort: bool (optional)
3415        :param index: The `index` parameter in the `export_variant_vcf` function is a boolean flag that
3416        determines whether or not to create an index for the output VCF file. If `index` is set to
3417        `True`, the output VCF file will be indexed using tabix. If `index`, defaults to False
3418        :type index: bool (optional)
3419        :param threads: The `threads` parameter in the `export_variant_vcf` function specifies the
3420        number of threads to use for exporting the VCF file. It determines how many parallel threads
3421        will be used during the export process. More threads can potentially speed up the export process
3422        by utilizing multiple cores of the processor. If
3423        :type threads: int | None
3424        :return: The `export_variant_vcf` function returns the result of calling the `export_output`
3425        method with various parameters including the output file, query, threads, sort flag, and index
3426        flag. The `export_output` method is responsible for exporting the VCF data based on the
3427        specified parameters and configurations provided in the `export_variant_vcf` function.
3428        """
3429
3430        # Config
3431        config = self.get_config()
3432
3433        # Extract VCF
3434        log.debug("Export VCF...")
3435
3436        # Table variants
3437        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
3438
3439        # Threads
3440        if not threads:
3441            threads = self.get_threads()
3442
3443        # Info fields
3444        if remove_info:
3445            if not isinstance(remove_info, str):
3446                remove_info = "."
3447            info_field = f"""'{remove_info}' as INFO"""
3448        else:
3449            info_field = "INFO"
3450
3451        # Samples fields
3452        if add_samples:
3453            if not list_samples:
3454                list_samples = self.get_header_sample_list()
3455            if list_samples:
3456                samples_fields = " , FORMAT , " + " , ".join(
3457                    [f""" "{sample}" """ for sample in list_samples]
3458                )
3459            else:
3460                samples_fields = ""
3461            log.debug(f"samples_fields: {samples_fields}")
3462        else:
3463            samples_fields = ""
3464
3465        # Where clause
3466        if where_clause is None:
3467            where_clause = ""
3468
3469        # Columns
3470        existing_columns = self.get_columns(table=table_variants)
3471        columns_default_values = {
3472            "#CHROM": "'chr'",
3473            "POS": "0",
3474            "ID": "'.'",
3475            "REF": "'N'",
3476            "ALT": "'N'",
3477            "QUAL": "'0'",
3478            "FILTER": "'PASS'",
3479        }
3480        select_fields_list = []
3481        for column in ["#CHROM", "POS", "ID", "REF", "ALT", "QUAL", "FILTER"]:
3482            if column not in existing_columns:
3483                select_fields_list.append(
3484                    f"{columns_default_values.get(column, '')} AS '{column}'"
3485                )
3486            else:
3487                select_fields_list.append(f'"{column}"')
3488        select_fields = ", ".join(select_fields_list)
3489
3490        # Query
3491        sql_query_select = f""" SELECT {select_fields}, {info_field} {samples_fields} FROM {table_variants} {where_clause} """
3492        log.debug(f"sql_query_select={sql_query_select}")
3493
3494        return self.export_output(
3495            output_file=vcf_file,
3496            output_header=None,
3497            export_header=True,
3498            explode_infos=False,
3499            query=sql_query_select,
3500            parquet_partitions=None,
3501            chunk_size=config.get("chunk_size", None),
3502            threads=threads,
3503            sort=sort,
3504            index=index,
3505            order_by=None,
3506        )
3507
3508    def run_commands(self, commands: list = [], threads: int = 1) -> None:
3509        """
3510        It takes a list of commands and runs them in parallel using the number of threads specified
3511
3512        :param commands: A list of commands to run
3513        :param threads: The number of threads to use, defaults to 1 (optional)
3514        """
3515
3516        run_parallel_commands(commands, threads)
3517
3518    def get_threads(self, default: int = 1) -> int:
3519        """
3520        This function returns the number of threads to use for a job, with a default value of 1 if not
3521        specified.
3522
3523        :param default: The `default` parameter in the `get_threads` method is used to specify the
3524        default number of threads to use if no specific value is provided. If no value is provided for
3525        the `threads` parameter in the configuration or input parameters, the `default` value will be
3526        used, defaults to 1
3527        :type default: int (optional)
3528        :return: the number of threads to use for the current job.
3529        """
3530
3531        # Config
3532        config = self.get_config()
3533
3534        # Param
3535        param = self.get_param()
3536
3537        # Input threads
3538        input_thread = param.get("threads", config.get("threads", None))
3539
3540        # Check threads
3541        if not input_thread:
3542            threads = default
3543        elif int(input_thread) <= 0:
3544            threads = os.cpu_count()
3545        else:
3546            threads = int(input_thread)
3547        return threads

3549    def get_memory_system(self, type: str = "available", unit: str = "G") -> str:
3550        """
3551        This function retrieves the system memory in the system and returns it as a string.
3552
3553        :param type: The `type` parameter in the `get_memory_system` function specifies the type of
3554        memory information to retrieve. It can take one of the following values: "total" to retrieve the
3555        total memory, "used" to retrieve the used memory, "percent" to retrieve the percentage of used memory,
3556        or "available" to retrieve the available memory. The default value is "available"
3557        :type type: str (optional)
3558        :param unit: The `unit` parameter in the `get_memory_system` function specifies the unit of
3559        measurement for the memory value. It can take one of the following values: "K" for kilobytes,
3560        "M" for megabytes, "G" for gigabytes, or "T" for terabytes. The default value is "G"
3561        :type unit: str (optional)
3562
3563        :return: The function `get_memory_system` returns a string representation of the available
3564        memory in the system.
3565        """
3566
3567        import psutil  # type: ignore
3568
3569        # Check system memory
3570        mem = psutil.virtual_memory()
3571
3572        # Get memory type
3573        if type == "total":
3574            memory = str(mem.total)
3575        elif type == "used":
3576            memory = str(mem.used)
3577        elif type == "percent":
3578            memory = str(mem.percent)
3579        elif type == "available":
3580            memory = str(mem.available)
3581        else:
3582            memory = str(mem.total)
3583
3584        # Convert unit
3585        unit_powers = {"K": 1, "M": 2, "G": 3, "T": 4}
3586        if unit in unit_powers:
3587            power = unit_powers[unit]
3588            memory = str(int(memory) // (1024**power))
3589
3590        # Return memory
3591        return f"{memory}{unit}"
3592
3593    def get_memory(self, default: str = None, available: bool = False) -> str:
3594        """
3595        This function retrieves the memory value from parameters or configuration with a default value
3596        if not found.
3597
3598        :param default: The `get_memory` function takes in a default value as a string parameter. This
3599        default value is used as a fallback in case the `memory` parameter is not provided in the
3600        `param` dictionary or the `config` dictionary. If `memory` is not found in either dictionary,
3601        the function
3602        :type default: str
3603        :param available: A boolean parameter that determines whether to limit the memory to the
3604        available system memory or not. If set to True, the function will return the minimum value
3605        between the input memory and the available system memory. If set to False, the function will
3606        return the input memory or the default value, defaults to False
3607        :type available: bool (optional)
3608        :return: The `get_memory` function returns a string value representing the memory parameter. If
3609        the `input_memory` is provided in the parameters, it will return that value. Otherwise, it will
3610        return the default value provided as an argument to the function.
3611        """
3612
3613        # Config
3614        config = self.get_config()
3615
3616        # Param
3617        param = self.get_param()
3618
3619        # Input threads
3620        input_memory = param.get("memory", config.get("memory", None))
3621
3622        # Avalable memory
3623        if available:
3624            available_memory = self.get_memory_system(type="available", unit="G")
3625            if available_memory is not None and input_memory is not None:
3626                input_memory = min(input_memory, available_memory)
3627            else:
3628                input_memory = available_memory
3629
3630        # Check threads
3631        if input_memory:
3632            memory = input_memory
3633        else:
3634            memory = default
3635
3636        return memory
3637
3638    def update_from_vcf(
3639        self,
3640        vcf_file: str,
3641        update_existing_fields: bool = False,
3642        remove_vcf_file: bool = True,
3643        upper_case: bool = True,
3644    ) -> None:
3645        """
3646        > If the database is duckdb, then use the parquet method, otherwise use the sqlite method
3647
3648        :param vcf_file: the path to the VCF file you want to update the database with
3649        :type vcf_file: str
3650        :param update_existing_fields: If True, existing fields in the INFO column will be updated
3651        with the values from the VCF file. If False, only new fields will be added, defaults to False
3652        :type update_existing_fields: bool (optional)
3653        :param remove_vcf_file: If True, the VCF file will be removed after the update is complete,
3654        defaults to True
3655        :type remove_vcf_file: bool (optional)
3656        :return: None
3657        """
3658
3659        connexion_format = self.get_connexion_format()
3660
3661        if connexion_format in ["duckdb"]:
3662            self.update_from_vcf_duckdb(
3663                vcf_file,
3664                update_existing_fields=update_existing_fields,
3665                remove_vcf_file=remove_vcf_file,
3666                upper_case=upper_case,
3667            )
3668        elif connexion_format in ["sqlite"]:
3669            self.update_from_vcf_sqlite(vcf_file)
3670
3671        if remove_vcf_file:
3672            remove_if_exists([vcf_file])
3673
3674    def update_from_vcf_duckdb(
3675        self,
3676        vcf_file: str,
3677        update_existing_fields: bool = False,
3678        remove_vcf_file: bool = True,
3679        upper_case: bool = True,
3680    ) -> None:
3681        """
3682        It takes a VCF file and updates the INFO column of the variants table in the database with the
3683        INFO column of the VCF file
3684
3685        :param vcf_file: The path to the VCF file you want to update the database with
3686        :type vcf_file: str
3687        :param update_existing_fields: If True, existing fields in the INFO column will be updated
3688        with the values from the VCF file. If False, only new fields will be added, defaults to False
3689        :type update_existing_fields: bool (optional)
3690        :param remove_vcf_file: If True, the VCF file will be removed after the update is complete,
3691        defaults to True
3692        :type remove_vcf_file: bool (optional)
3693        :param upper_case: If True, the ALT and REF fields will be compared in uppercase, defaults to True
3694        :type upper_case: bool (optional)
3695        :return: None
3696        """
3697
3698        # variants table
3699        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
3700
3701        # Connexion
3702        conn = self.get_connexion()
3703
3704        log.info(f"Update variants table from file '{os.path.basename(vcf_file)}'...")
3705
3706        with TemporaryDirectory(dir=self.get_tmp_dir()) as tmp_dir:
3707
3708            log.debug(f"Create parquet files from VCF '{vcf_file}'...")
3709
3710            # Create parquet from VCF
3711            vcf_file_parquet_path = os.path.join(tmp_dir, "vcf_file.parquet")
3712            vcf_file_parquet = Variants(
3713                input=vcf_file, load=True, config={"access": "RO"}
3714            )
3715
3716            log.debug(f"Variants input format '{vcf_file_parquet.get_input_format()}'")
3717
3718            if vcf_file_parquet.get_input_format() == "parquet":
3719
3720                # list of parquet files
3721                vcf_file_parquet_path = vcf_file
3722
3723            else:
3724
3725                # Export parquet parameters
3726                chunk_size = self.get_config().get("chunk_size", None)
3727                threads = self.get_threads()
3728
3729                # Export parquet files
3730                log.debug("Export VCF to partitioned parquet...")
3731                vcf_file_parquet.export_output(
3732                    output_file=vcf_file_parquet_path,
3733                    chunk_size=chunk_size,
3734                    threads=threads,
3735                    export_header=True,
3736                )
3737                log.debug(f"Parquet generated: {vcf_file_parquet_path}")
3738
3739                if remove_vcf_file:
3740                    remove_if_exists([vcf_file])
3741
3742            # Update if fields exist
3743            if update_existing_fields:
3744                # list of header columns
3745                header_columns = self.get_header().infos.keys()
3746                header_columns_vcf_file_parquet = (
3747                    vcf_file_parquet.get_header().infos.keys()
3748                )
3749
3750                # columns that exist in both
3751                common_columns = list(
3752                    set(header_columns).intersection(
3753                        set(header_columns_vcf_file_parquet)
3754                    )
3755                )
3756
3757                # Remove common columns
3758                if len(common_columns) > 0:
3759                    log.debug(f"Common columns to update/remove: {common_columns}")
3760                    self.rename_info_fields(
3761                        fields_to_rename=dict.fromkeys(common_columns, None)
3762                    )
3763                else:
3764                    log.debug("No common columns to update/remove")
3765
3766            # Upper case function for ALT and REF
3767            if upper_case:
3768                upper_func = "upper"
3769            else:
3770                upper_func = ""
3771
3772            # Create table/view from parquet files
3773            table_source_name = "table_parquet_" + get_random(10)
3774            sql_query_update = f"""
3775                CREATE VIEW {table_source_name}
3776                AS (
3777                    SELECT "#CHROM", POS, {upper_func}(REF) as REF, {upper_func}(ALT) as ALT, INFO
3778                    FROM read_parquet('{vcf_file_parquet_path}')
3779                    WHERE INFO NOT IN ('','.')
3780                )
3781                ;
3782            """
3783            # log.debug(f"sql_query_update: {sql_query_update}")
3784            conn.execute(sql_query_update)
3785
3786            # Update INFO fields with update_table function
3787            source = {
3788                "table": table_source_name,
3789                "join_keys": ["#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT"],
3790                "columns": {
3791                    "INFO": {
3792                        "columns": ["INFO"],
3793                        "mode": "append",
3794                        "separator": ";",
3795                    }
3796                },
3797            }
3798            self.update_table(
3799                dest_table=table_variants,
3800                sources=[source],
3801                physical_order=True,
3802                force_strategy=None,
3803                upper_case=upper_case,
3804            )
3805
3806            return None
3807
3808    def update_from_vcf_sqlite(self, vcf_file: str) -> None:
3809        """
3810        It creates a temporary table in the SQLite database, loads the VCF file into the temporary
3811        table, then updates the INFO column of the variants table with the INFO column of the temporary
3812        table
3813
3814        :param vcf_file: The path to the VCF file you want to update the database with
3815        """
3816
3817        # Create a temporary table for the VCF
3818        table_vcf = "tmp_vcf"
3819        sql_create = (
3820            f"CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE {table_vcf} AS SELECT * FROM variants WHERE 0"
3821        )
3822        self.conn.execute(sql_create)
3823
3824        # Loading VCF into temporaire table
3825        vcf_df = pd.read_csv(
3826            vcf_file, sep="\t", comment="#", header=None, low_memory=False
3827        )
3828        vcf_df.columns = ["#CHROM", "POS", "ID", "REF", "ALT", "QUAL", "FILTER", "INFO"]
3829        vcf_df.to_sql(table_vcf, self.conn, if_exists="append", index=False)
3830
3831        # Update table 'variants' with VCF data
3832        # warning: CONCAT as || operator
3833        sql_query_update = f"""
3834            UPDATE variants as table_variants
3835            SET INFO = CASE
3836                            WHEN INFO NOT IN ('', '.')
3837                            THEN INFO
3838                            ELSE ''
3839                        END ||
3840                        (
3841                        SELECT 
3842                            CASE 
3843                                WHEN table_variants.INFO NOT IN ('','.') 
3844                                    AND table_vcf.INFO NOT IN ('','.')  
3845                                THEN ';' 
3846                                ELSE '' 
3847                            END || 
3848                            CASE 
3849                                WHEN table_vcf.INFO NOT IN ('','.') 
3850                                THEN table_vcf.INFO 
3851                                ELSE '' 
3852                            END
3853                        FROM {table_vcf} as table_vcf
3854                        WHERE table_vcf.\"#CHROM\" = table_variants.\"#CHROM\"
3855                            AND table_vcf.\"POS\" = table_variants.\"POS\"
3856                            AND table_vcf.\"ALT\" = table_variants.\"ALT\"
3857                            AND table_vcf.\"REF\" = table_variants.\"REF\"
3858                        )
3859        """
3860        self.conn.execute(sql_query_update)
3861
3862        # Drop temporary table
3863        sql_drop = f"DROP TABLE {table_vcf}"
3864        self.conn.execute(sql_drop)
3865
3866    def drop_variants_table(self) -> None:
3867        """
3868        > This function drops the variants table
3869        """
3870
3871        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
3872        sql_table_variants = f"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {table_variants}"
3873        self.conn.execute(sql_table_variants)

3875    def set_variant_id(
3876        self, variant_id_column: str = "variant_id", force: bool = None
3877    ) -> str:
3878        """
3879        It adds a column to the variants table called `variant_id` and populates it with a hash of the
3880        `#CHROM`, `POS`, `REF`, and `ALT` columns
3881
3882        :param variant_id_column: The name of the column to be created in the variants table, defaults
3883        to variant_id
3884        :type variant_id_column: str (optional)
3885        :param force: If True, the variant_id column will be created even if it already exists
3886        :type force: bool
3887        :return: The name of the column that contains the variant_id
3888        """
3889
3890        # Assembly
3891        assembly = self.get_param().get(
3892            "assembly", self.get_config().get("assembly", DEFAULT_ASSEMBLY)
3893        )
3894
3895        # INFO/Tag prefix
3896        prefix = self.get_explode_infos_prefix()
3897
3898        # Explode INFO/SVTYPE
3899        added_columns = self.explode_infos(prefix=prefix, fields=["SVTYPE"])
3900
3901        # variants table
3902        table_variants = self.get_table_variants()
3903
3904        # variant_id column
3905        if not variant_id_column:
3906            variant_id_column = "variant_id"
3907
3908        # Creta variant_id column
3909        if "variant_id" not in self.get_extra_infos() or force:
3910
3911            # Create column
3912            self.add_column(
3913                table_name=table_variants,
3914                column_name=variant_id_column,
3915                column_type="UBIGINT",
3916                default_value="0",
3917            )
3918
3919            # Update column
3920            self.conn.execute(f"""
3921                    UPDATE {table_variants}
3922                    SET "{variant_id_column}" = hash('{assembly}', "#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT", '"{prefix}SVTYPE"')
3923                """)
3924
3925        # Remove added columns
3926        for added_column in added_columns:
3927            self.drop_column(column=added_column)
3928
3929        # return variant_id column name
3930        return variant_id_column
3931
3932    def get_variant_id_column(
3933        self, variant_id_column: str = "variant_id", force: bool = None
3934    ) -> str:
3935        """
3936        This function returns the variant_id column name
3937
3938        :param variant_id_column: The name of the column in the dataframe that contains the variant IDs,
3939        defaults to variant_id
3940        :type variant_id_column: str (optional)
3941        :param force: If True, will force the variant_id to be set to the value of variant_id_column. If
3942        False, will only set the variant_id if it is not already set. If None, will set the variant_id
3943        if it is not already set, or if it is set
3944        :type force: bool
3945        :return: The variant_id column name.
3946        """
3947
3948        return self.set_variant_id(variant_id_column=variant_id_column, force=force)

3950    def get_columns_type(self, table: str) -> dict:
3951        """
3952        Get columns type of a table.
3953        :param table: The `table` parameter is a string that represents the name of the table
3954        for which you want to retrieve the column types.
3955        :type table: str
3956        :return: The function `get_columns_type` returns a dictionary where the keys are the
3957        column names of the specified table and the values are the corresponding data types of
3958        those columns.
3959        """
3960
3961        # Get columns info
3962        query = f"""
3963            PRAGMA table_info('{table}')
3964        """
3965        df_columns = self.get_query_to_df(query)
3966
3967        # Construct columns type dict
3968        columns_type = {}
3969        for _, row in df_columns.iterrows():
3970            columns_type[row["name"]] = row["type"]
3971
3972        return columns_type

4330    def get_config_json(
4331        self, name: str, config_dict: dict = {}, config_file: str = None
4332    ) -> dict:
4333        """
4334        The function `get_config_json` retrieves a configuration JSON object with prioritizations from
4335        default values, a dictionary, and a file.
4336
4337        :param name: The `name` parameter in the `get_config_json` function is a string that represents
4338        the name of the configuration. It is used to identify and retrieve the configuration settings
4339        for a specific component or module
4340        :type name: str
4341        :param config_dict: The `config_dict` parameter in the `get_config_json` function is a
4342        dictionary that allows you to provide additional configuration settings or overrides. When you
4343        call the `get_config_json` function, you can pass a dictionary containing key-value pairs where
4344        the key is the configuration setting you want to override or
4345        :type config_dict: dict
4346        :param config_file: The `config_file` parameter in the `get_config_json` function is used to
4347        specify the path to a configuration file that contains additional settings. If provided, the
4348        function will read the contents of this file and update the configuration dictionary with the
4349        values found in the file, overriding any existing values with the
4350        :type config_file: str
4351        :return: The function `get_config_json` returns a dictionary containing the configuration
4352        settings.
4353        """
4354
4355        # Create with default prioritizations
4356        config_default = self.get_config_default(name=name)
4357        configuration = config_default
4358        # log.debug(f"configuration={configuration}")
4359
4360        # Replace prioritizations from dict
4361        for config in config_dict:
4362            configuration[config] = config_dict[config]
4363
4364        # Replace prioritizations from file
4365        config_file = full_path(config_file)
4366        if config_file:
4367            if os.path.exists(config_file):
4368                with open(config_file) as config_file_content:
4369                    config_file_dict = yaml.safe_load(config_file_content)
4370                for config in config_file_dict:
4371                    configuration[config] = config_file_dict[config]
4372            else:
4373                msg_error = f"Config '{name}' file '{config_file}' does NOT exist"
4374                log.error(msg_error)
4375                raise ValueError(msg_error)
4376
4377        return configuration
4378
4379    def prioritization(
4380        self,
4381        table: str = None,
4382        pz_prefix: str = None,
4383        pz_param: dict = None,
4384        pz_keys: list = None,
4385        strict: bool = False,
4386    ) -> bool:
4387        """
4388        Processes VCF files, adds new INFO fields, and prioritizes variants based on configured profiles and criteria.
4389
4390        Args:
4391            table (str, optional): The name of the table (presumably a VCF file) on which the prioritization operation will be performed.
4392                If not provided, the default variants table will be used.
4393            pz_prefix (str, optional): A prefix to be added to certain INFO fields in the VCF file during the prioritization process.
4394                Defaults to "PZ" if not provided.
4395            pz_param (dict, optional): Additional parameters specific to the prioritization process. These parameters can include settings
4396                related to prioritization profiles, fields, scoring modes, flags, comments, and other configurations needed for the prioritization
4397                of variants.
4398            pz_keys (list, optional): The keys used to join the prioritization table with the variant table. Defaults to ["#CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT"]
4399                if not provided.
4400            strict (bool, optional): Whether to enforce strict prioritization criteria availability in view (need to be in header and in column). Defaults to False.
4401
4402        Returns:
4403            bool: True if the prioritization operation is successful, False otherwise.
4404        """
4405
4406        # Config
4407        config = self.get_config()
4408
4409        # Param
4410        param = self.get_param()
4411
4412        # Prioritization param
4413        if pz_param is not None:
4414            prioritization_param = pz_param
4415        else:
4416            prioritization_param = param.get("prioritization", {})
4417
4418        # Configuration profiles

4420            "prioritization_config", None
4421        )

4423        prioritizations_config = self.get_config_json(
4424            name="prioritizations", config_file=prioritization_config_file
4425        )
4426
4427        # Prioritization prefix
4428        pz_prefix_default = "PZ"
4429        if pz_prefix is None:
4430            pz_prefix = prioritization_param.get("pzprefix", pz_prefix_default)
4431
4432        # Prioritization options
4433        profiles = prioritization_param.get("profiles", [])
4434        if isinstance(profiles, str):
4435            profiles = profiles.split(",")
4436        pzfields = prioritization_param.get(
4437            "pzfields", [f"{pz_prefix}Flag", f"{pz_prefix}Score"]
4438        )
4439        if isinstance(pzfields, str):
4440            pzfields = pzfields.split(",")

4449        if prioritizations:

4455
4456        # Keys for prioritization join

4459
4460        # If profile "ALL" provided, all profiles in the config profiles

4462            profiles = list(prioritizations_config.keys())
4463
4464        for profile in profiles:

4466                log.debug(f"Profile '{profile}' configured")

4471
4472        if profiles:

4477
4478        if not default_profile and len(profiles):

4945                                        f"{pz_prefix}Flag{pzfields_sep}{profile} = {pz_prefix}Flag{pzfields_sep}{profile} AND {criterion_flag_bool}"
4946                                    )

4951                                    in list_of_pzfields
4952                                    and criterion_class is not None
4953                                ):
4954                                    sql_set.append(
4955                                        f" {pz_prefix}Class{pzfields_sep}{profile} = list_concat(list_distinct({pz_prefix}Class{pzfields_sep}{profile}), {criterion_class}) "
4956                                    )
4957

4960                                    f"{pz_prefix}Comment{pzfields_sep}{profile}"
4961                                    in list_of_pzfields
4962                                ):

4967                                                    CASE

4969                                                        THEN ', '

4971                                                    END,

4984                                                    {pz_prefix}Infos{pzfields_sep}{profile},
4985                                                    '{criterion_infos}'
4986                                                )
4987                                        """)
4988                                sql_set_option = ",".join(sql_set)
4989
4990                                # Criterion and comparison
4991                                if sql_set_option:
4992
4993                                    # Operation mode
4994                                    if criterion_mode in ["operation"]:
4995
4996                                        # Check if value is a float
4997                                        try:
4998
4999                                            # Test if criterion is a float
5000                                            float(criterion_value)
5001

5010
5011                                            sql_update = f"""

5019                                                        AND   CAST("{annotation_view_name}"."{annotations_view_prefix}{annotation}" AS FLOAT){comparison_map[criterion_type]}{criterion_value}
5020                                                        )
5021                                                    ) AS "{annotation_view_name}"
5022                                                WHERE ({" AND ".join(clause_join)})
5023                                                
5024                                            """
5025                                        # If not a float
5026                                        except:
5027                                            contains_option = ""
5028                                            if criterion_type == "contains":
5029                                                contains_option = ".*"
5030                                            sql_update = f"""
5031                                                UPDATE "{table_variants}"
5032                                                SET {sql_set_option}
5033                                                FROM (
5034                                                    SELECT *
5035                                                    FROM "{annotation_view_name}"
5036                                                    WHERE (

5038                                                        )

5040                                                WHERE ({" AND ".join(clause_join)})
5041                                                  
5042                                            """

5044
5045                                    # SQL mode

5047
5048                                        sql_update = f"""

5051                                            FROM (
5052                                                SELECT *
5053                                                FROM "{annotation_view_name}"
5054                                                WHERE ({criterion_sql})
5055                                                ) AS "{annotation_view_name}"
5056                                            WHERE ({" AND ".join(clause_join)})
5057                                        """
5058                                        sql_queries.append(sql_update)
5059
5060                                    else:

5062                                        log.error(msg_err)
5063                                        raise ValueError(msg_err)
5064
5065                                else:

5067                                        f"NO SQL SET option for '{annotation}' - '{criterion}'"
5068                                    )
5069
5070                        # PZTags
5071                        if (
5072                            f"{pz_prefix}Tags{pzfields_sep}{profile}"
5073                            in list_of_pzfields
5074                        ):

5092                                        elif pzfield in [f"{pz_prefix}Class"]:
5093                                            pztags_value += f"""{pztags_sep}{pzfield}#',

5096                                                    ELSE '.'
5097                                                END, '"""
5098                                        else:

5100                                        pztags_sep = pztags_sep_default
5101
5102                            # Add Query update for PZFlags

5112                                    )

5131
5132                        # Chromosomes list

5136                        """
5137                        chroms = self.get_query_to_df(sql_uniq_chrom)["#CHROM"].tolist()
5138

5140

5146
5147                                # Query num

5152

5155
5156                                    sql_query_chrom = f"""

5168                        # Update INFO field

5170                        sql_query_update = f"""

5187
5188        else:

5191
